summary: A queue is a linear collection with FIFO (first in, first out) access: items leave in the order they arrived. Enqueue adds at the rear and dequeue removes from the front.

sections.heading: Operations
bullets: enqueue(x): add at the rear. O(1).
dequeue(): remove and return the front. O(1) with the right implementation.

sections.heading: Simple array queue and the dead-space problem
sections.body: With `front` and `rear` indices that only move forward, slots before `front` are never reused. After several dequeues the queue reports full even though it has free space at the start. Shifting everything left on each dequeue fixes it but costs O(n). The circular queue is the clean fix.

sections.heading: Linked-list queue
sections.body: Keep head (front) and tail (rear) pointers. Enqueue appends at the tail, dequeue removes at the head, both O(1) with no capacity limit.

sections.heading: Applications
bullets: CPU and disk scheduling (round-robin ready queue).
Buffering between producer and consumer: keyboard, network packets, print jobs.
Breadth-first search and level-order tree traversal.

subtopics.title: Deque (double-ended queue)
subtopics.summary: Insert and remove at both ends.

sections.body: A deque supports push/pop at front and back in O(1). It generalizes both stack and queue and enables sliding-window maximum with a monotonic deque.
Dequeue returns the highest-priority item. A binary heap gives O(log n) insert and extract. Used for scheduling, Dijkstra, and event simulation.
A bounded blocking queue lets producers wait when full and consumers wait when empty, decoupling speeds. Lock-free ring buffers are used in networking drivers and audio.
Push onto an `in` stack; when `out` is empty, pop everything from `in` onto `out`. Each element moves at most once, so amortized O(1) per operation.

bullets: Simple (linear) queue: FIFO with the dead-space problem.
Circular queue: wraps indices to reuse space.
Deque: insert and remove at both ends.
Priority queue: dequeue by priority, usually a heap.
Blocking and concurrent queues: thread-safe producer-consumer buffers.

takeaways: FIFO: enqueue at rear, dequeue at front.
A naive array queue wastes space; use a circular buffer or linked list.
Queues drive BFS, scheduling, and buffering.
Know deque and priority queue as variants.
